note: PROVISIONAL. Unlike rollback_completion_bounds.json, these values are enforced: the core compiles the same numbers in (IngressLimits::DECLARED in rust/azazel-edge-core/src/ingress.rs) and a core unit test fails if the two differ. The core does not read this file at run time. Not hardware evidence, and not a program-plan section 8 target: those are unchanged.

quotas.applies_to: non-alert EVE lines only. Alerts are never shed and never rate-limited; they are bounded per poll only (alerts_per_poll, examine_per_poll, poll_work_limit_ms) so the release sweep runs between polls, and the next poll follows at once when a budget stopped the last one.
quotas.excess_policy: A non-alert line that finds the token bucket below its class reserve is shed at once: flow keeps 3/8 of the burst in reserve, dns 2/8, stats 1/8, other and unparseable none, so flow is shed first, then dns, then stats. As a second line, past backlog_bound_bytes of unread file flow is shed whatever the bucket holds, and each further multiple of the bound adds dns, stats, then every other non-alert type. Unparseable lines (they might have been alerts) share the last rank and are counted apart. Lines longer than max_line_bytes are skipped to their newline and counted (oversized_lines_skipped, oversized_possible_alerts). Past alert_backlog_bound_bytes an ingress_alert_backlog summary is recorded and alerts keep being read. Counts leave the core as at most one ingress_shed summary per audit interval in ingress-audit.jsonl (0600, O_NOFOLLOW, fsync per record, rotated to .1 at audit_log_cap_bytes) beside the normalized event log, and on stdout (stderr when AZAZEL_EVENT_STDOUT=off).

basis.method: release build of azazel-edge-core on main at 4b5242c (decision path unchanged by OF-06; the old reader had no bound), Edge defaults, enforcement off, AI forward off, stdout off, normalized log on: 200000 pre-written synthetic EVE alerts (the SO-04 harness's eve_flood line shape, about 300 bytes each) read from the start of the file, time until all 200000 decisions were in the normalized log; docker on colima, aarch64 (image edge414-ci:py311)
basis.margin_rule: non-alert quota: less than half the minimum observed sustained alert decision rate (a non-alert line costs no more than an alert: it is parsed but not decided), rounded down to the next 500 lines/s, leaving at least half the measured capacity for alerts
basis.per_poll_rule: alerts_per_poll 1000: at the measured per-alert cost (130-177 us uncontended, up to about 300 us with other containers on the VM) one poll's alert work is about 0.13-0.3 s, far below the SO-04 5 s bounds; poll_work_limit_ms 500 caps it on a slower host. Polls that stop on a budget are not followed by the 200 ms sleep, so alert throughput stays near the measured capacity (see alert_throughput_check). non_alert_burst is 0.6 s of the quota; examine_per_poll is four times non_alert_burst
basis.backlog_rule: backlog_bound_bytes (8 MiB) is several seconds of the quota at real EVE line sizes; alert_backlog_bound_bytes (256 MiB) is a hard record point, not a drop point
basis.contended_check: Re-measured the same way the same day while other containers ran on the same 2-CPU colima VM (main binary, 60000-line backlog, decisions over 8 s): 5252, 3348 and 3957 lines/s. All exceed the non-alert quota.
basis.alert_throughput_check: Same container, 60000-alert backlog, decisions over 8 s, three alternating runs: main 6530, 6495, 6529 alerts/s; this tree 6502, 6504, 6524 alerts/s. Alerts are not throttled below capacity.
basis.so04_check: SO-04 harness re-run twice on this tree (eve_flood 2000 alerts/s; alerts are outside the quota): start max 1119.8 and 1833.7 ms (bound 5000 ms), completion max 1071.8 and 1458.8 ms over all action types (provisional bounds 5000 ms), 0 violations, 150/150 samples per part in both runs.
